entries.test: Whether published studies show LLM accuracy drops on items outside their training distribution or on subtle variants of familiar problems, compared with familiar items.
entries.note: A general empirical claim about generalisation, backed by a large literature on contamination and perturbed benchmarks.
Whether LLMs 'literally don't reason' depends on contested definitions of reasoning. Only the riddle-specific failure could be checked.

entries.test: Whether any general-purpose LLM is shown to work reliably, for example with near-zero hallucination and error rates across broad independent evaluations.
entries.note: He states this as a 'strong intuition', which is a firm expectation, not a probability. 'Never' means only a reliable general LLM could settle it, by proving it false.

entries.test: Whether there are documented arithmetic errors, fabrications and similar failures for every major transformer model released from GPT-2 through SearchGPT.
entries.note: The pattern of errors can be checked. The claim that a lack of sanity-checking causes them is harder to verify.

entries.test: Whether studies of LLM reasoning and planning (for example perturbed planning or maths benchmarks) show performance that is good near the training distribution and degrades sharply away from it.
entries.note: This reflects models as of mid-2024.

entries.test: Whether LLMs available as of July 2024 still produced hallucinations and basic reasoning errors, as documented by evaluations and reported incidents.
entries.note: The 'inevitable' part is hedged with 'as far as I can tell' and is harder to test. The 'not yet disappeared' part is plainly checkable.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI's public research and product releases up to mid-2024 focused mainly on scaling LLMs, with symbolic components such as tools or code execution only minor or not highlighted.
entries.note: 'Dogma' and 'hide them behind the curtain' are loaded wording and partly about motive. Only the description of where OpenAI put its effort is graded.

entries.test: Whether frontier models from the major labs in mid-2024 clustered at roughly GPT-4-level benchmark performance and still hallucinated, and whether major companies' AI investment went overwhelmingly into scaling LLMs.
entries.note: The normalised wording softens 'exactly the same thing' slightly, but 'for the most part' keeps the hedge.
This is a claim about what progress toward AGI requires: neurosymbolic methods are necessary but not sufficient. There is no shared test for 'a necessary step on a longer journey'.
